name: Salkyn-Tor National Park
near: Alysh village (the park's address in 2GIS) and the town of Naryn: according to CBT Naryn the park is ~12 km east of Naryn (Nomad's Land — 18 km, Lonely Planet — 17 km); from the arch on the main road to the entrance is ~2 km.
elev: About 2200 m at the entrance (Nomad's Land); the CBT Naryn trail starts at 2167 m, and the highest point of the route, by the glacier, is 3221 m.
short: A 10,448-hectare nature park on the northern slope of the Naryn-Too range near Naryn: Schrenk spruce forests, a river with footbridges, a picnic area at the entrance and a 13 km trail to a glacier; it was created to protect the maral (Tian Shan red deer).
desc: Salkyn-Tor (“cool peak”) is a state nature park established in May 2001 on the northern slope of the Naryn-Too range, roughly 12–18 km east of Naryn, covering 10,448 hectares. Its main purpose is restoring the Tian Shan maral population; roe deer, lynx, brown bear, wolf, stone marten, ibex and marmots also live here, along with Red Data Book species. The lower belt is dense Schrenk spruce forest with Tian Shan rowan, wild rose and barberry. At the entrance are a picnic area, toilets, small cabins and yurts (partly abandoned according to reviews), and the famous bridge shaped like the letter “M” (the “lovers' bridge”). The main trail goes up the river valley: the first 2 km have three footbridges, then come fords, around km 10 there is a shepherds' camp in the spruce forest, and above it a rocky climb to the fork of the river and the glacier (13 km, 2167 → 3221 m). The territory also has the Kojo-Ungur cave, the historic Dubolu hill, the Kurga spring, and the Kok-Jayyk, Berkut-Uya and Kyzyl-Zoo canyons; the area has about 30 hot and cold springs.
guide: For an easy day the lower zone is enough: a picnic by the river, a walk across the three footbridges and a photo on the “M” bridge — it's a favorite weekend spot for Naryn residents. For a real hike, set out early and walk 13 km up to the glacier — the way to the shepherds' camp in the spruce forest (~10 km) is level, after which the rocky climb begins. Be ready to take your shoes off at the fords, and in June to cross the river on snow bridges, testing them with a stick. Entry is paid, so keep cash on hand. Take your trash with you — reviews complain about dirty picnic areas.
see: Schrenk spruce forests in the river valley; the footbridges and the “M” bridge at the entrance; the shepherds' camp in the spruce forest (~10 km); the glacier and the upper fork of the river (3221 m); the Kojo-Ungur cave, Dubolu hill, the Kurga spring, the Kok-Jayyk, Berkut-Uya and Kyzyl-Zoo canyons; nearby — the maral nursery (Pitomnik Bugu Maralov).
skip: You have already seen the spruce forests of Jeti-Oguz/Ala-Archa and aren't up for the full 26 km route — the lower zone is modest and littered in places. You're only passing through Naryn on the way to Tash-Rabat and have less than 3–4 hours. You're going in early summer with no experience of fords — the upper part of the trail with snow bridges is dangerous.
diff: The lower walking zone is easy (picnic, footbridges). The full CBT Naryn route is hard but not technical: 13 km one way, ~1690 m of ascent, several fords, rocky upper reaches; in early summer, snow bridges.
when: July–September for the full trail (at the end of June there is still snow and snow bridges over the river — CBT Naryn); the lower zone from late May to October. In summer it is popular with locals on weekends — quieter on weekdays.
hours: No official opening hours are published (2GIS, Google — hours not given). Entry is paid, with a check at the barrier/arch; ask CBT Naryn (+996 559 567 685).
daytime: An early start (7–8 am) for the glacier route — 26 km round trip; a picnic works any time of day. In the daytime the water at the fords is higher because of melting.
how: From Naryn east along the road beside the Naryn River toward the airport and At-Bashy for ~12–18 km to the arch by the main road (Alysh village area), then ~2 km to the entrance. From Bishkek to Naryn — 4.5–5 h (marshrutka (minibus) 600 som, GoBus 500 som).
needcar: Yes: from Naryn 12–18 km — taxi or car; on foot from the arch to the entrance is 2 km. The sources mention no public transport to the entrance (Naryn — At-Bashy marshrutkas may drop you at the arch — not confirmed).
self: Yes: the trail is obvious, along the river; there is a fee at the entrance. For the upper part beyond the shepherds' camp (the trail fades, snow) a guide or experience is better; central-asia.guide recommends a guide for the park's remote sites.
roadtype: Paved Naryn — At-Bashy highway to the arch; ~2 km of access road to the entrance (surface not given in the sources). Inside, a footpath: bridges in the first 2 km, then fords and a rocky trail.
traveltime: Naryn — park entrance ~20–30 min (12–18 km; estimate). The full route to the glacier is 13 km one way, a full daylight day round trip. To the shepherds' camp (~10 km) — 3–4 h (estimate).
stay: At the entrance there are small cabins and yurts (Lonely Planet; partly abandoned according to TripAdvisor reviews) and Soviet-era recreation bases with yurts and simple cabins (central-asia.guide) — prices are not published. Usonbak Yurt Camp in the Salkyn-Tor area is mentioned on TripAdvisor (prices not found). The main option is guesthouses and hotels in Naryn via CBT Naryn; camping in the park is with the administration's permission (not confirmed).
net: Not confirmed by sources. In Naryn and along the highway there is Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage; deeper in the gorge the signal probably drops out — an offline map is essential.
entry: Entry is paid (TripAdvisor reviews). Nomad's Land gives $1 per person (year not stated). The current 2025–2026 tariff in som is not confirmed; in June 2026 a member of the Jogorku Kenesh proposed charging foreigners $20–50 to enter national parks — no decision has been made (Vesti.kg, 22.06.2026).
transfer: No published taxi prices Naryn — Salkyn-Tor were found; a car via CBT Naryn is on request. Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (May 2026), GoBus 500 som (2024).
bring: Shoes you don't mind getting wet, or sandals, for the fords; trekking poles (snow bridges in June); warm clothes for the upper part (3221 m); water and food for the whole day; cash for the entrance; a bag for trash.
warn: Fords across the river; in June, snow bridges that can collapse (CBT Naryn). Above the shepherds' camp the trail fades. Brown bears and wolves live in the park — don't leave food in your tent. Trash and dirt at the picnic areas by the entrance (reviews).
food: No cafes in the park are confirmed — bring food for a picnic. In Naryn you'll find the national dishes of Naryn region: beshbarmak, naryn (thin noodles with meat), and kumys in summer; at the shepherds' camps on the route, kumys and ayran (by arrangement).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.7/5, 25 ratings (03.10.2026). 2GIS: 4.9/5, 27 reviews (viewed 07.10.2026). TripAdvisor: 4.8/5, 12 reviews. Pros: beautiful mountains and spruce forests, family trails, convenient from Naryn, the “M” bridge. Cons: trash, abandoned picnic areas, fords where you have to take your shoes off, an entry fee with no stated tariff.
p.sum: Salkyn-Tor is the nearest nature to Naryn: 12–20 km east along the paved road toward At-Bashy, then ~2 km to the entrance; from town, a taxi or a CBT Naryn car (20–30 min). Entry is paid but token (20 som per Wikivoyage/Journal of Nomads; the current 2026 tariff is not confirmed). For an easy day: a picnic and the footbridges at the entrance; for a hike: 13 km to the glacier with 1690 m of ascent (a full daylight day, fords). It's more convenient to stay overnight in Naryn: guesthouses from $8–10 to $50 on Booking, CBT Naryn ≈600 som with breakfast.

p.season: May–June: the lower zone is accessible, above it there is snow and snow bridges. July–September: the full route. Summer weekends — lots of locals. October: cold, lower zone. Winter: snow.
p.budget.economy: ≈2000–3000 som/person: marshrutka Bishkek — Naryn 600×2, taxi to the park (negotiable), entry 20 som, guesthouse $8–10.
p.budget.comfort: Car/guide via CBT Naryn (on request), hotel $40–70.
p.permits: No permit needed. Entry is paid: 20 som/person (Journal of Nomads 2024, Wikivoyage) or $1 (Nomad's Land); the 2026 tariff is not confirmed.
p.access: The lower zone is fine with children and older people; with a stroller, only the areas at the entrance. The full route is for prepared hikers.
